ImageDescription.value: A Nile Crocodile on the banks of the Masai River. You can hardly see that he is there. Although fish form a major part of their diet, Nile Crocodiles kill and consume several of the migrating animals during the Great Migration.  Among the mammals, prey consists of gazelles, antelope, waterbuck, sitatunga, lechwe, wildebeest, zebras, warthogs, young hippos, giraffes,[18] Cape buffalos,[18] and young elephants. When given the chance, they are known to prey on domestic chickens, goats, sheep and cattle. Nile crocodiles also prey on humans frequently, far more often than other crocodilian species. Their usual technique is to bite onto the unfortunate victim's leg and drag it under water so that it will drown. (Oct/ Nov 2010)
